rituals.title: WORD MELT
rituals.goal: Repeat the sound until the spell loses its language.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose Charged — Choose one charged word—not a whole painful story.
2. Say Gently — Say it gently and steadily for about twenty seconds.
3. Listen Moment — Listen for the moment it becomes rhythm, mouth movement, or noise.
4. Stop Room — Stop there and look around the room.
5. Return Seen — Meaning may return; you have seen it separate once.
rituals.win: ✓ The word lost its spell; I heard sound without obeying meaning.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Return Seen”; leave the forecast.
• If it flares, choose “Listen Moment”.
• “Stop Room” — fear isn’t fate.
• Look back: “Choose Charged” → “Return Seen”.
• I can use “Say Gently” while fear stays loud.
rituals.formula_flow: Choose Charged → Say Gently → Listen Moment → Stop Room → Return Seen
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Avoid this with slurs, trauma phrases, voices, or material that escalates symptoms.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: ONE INCH BEYOND EASY
rituals.goal: Competence grows at the edge, not at the cliff.
rituals.steps:
1. Select Task — Select a task you can already do.
2. Increase — Increase one dimension slightly: duration, complexity, independence, or visibility.
3. Complete Version — Complete that version and note what skill carried you through.
4. Raise One Inch — The next challenge must be earned by evidence, not demanded by shame.
rituals.win: ✓ Made the next challenge earn its place with evidence.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Raise One Inch”; release extra blame.
• Re-entry move: “Complete Version”.
• “Complete Version” keeps blame in proportion.
• What changed: “Select Task” → “Raise One Inch”?
• I can use “Increase” without owning everything.

rituals.title: THEN / NOW SUBTITLES
rituals.goal: Flashbacks need temporal translation.
rituals.steps:
1. Alternate Lines — When memory body alarm begins, alternate lines: THEN—state one past fact; NOW—state one current difference.
2. Include Age — Include age, place, available help, bodily freedom, and exits.
3. Keep Eyes — Keep eyes open and touch the environment after every pair.
4. Date Location — The screen may replay; the subtitles restore date and location.
rituals.win: ✓ Gave the replay a date and location instead of letting it become now.
rituals.supports:
• Gently exhale after “Date Location”; orient to now.
• Pulled back? Touch “Keep Eyes”.
• “Keep Eyes” moves memory toward then.
• What changed: “Alternate Lines” → “Date Location”?
• I can use “Include Age” while staying in now.

rituals.title: ENOUGH IS A CURRENT FACT
rituals.goal: Sufficiency can coexist with ambition.
rituals.steps:
1. Identify Part — Spot one part of the present condition that is really adequate: shelter, breath, effort, support, knowledge, or time for the next step.
2. Receive Adequacy — Receive that adequacy without claiming everything is fine.
3. Choose Non — From this base, choose one non-desperate improvement.
rituals.win: ✓ I found one thing that was already enough, then chose from there.
rituals.supports:
• Gently exhale after “Choose Non”; no forcing.
• On return, repeat “Receive Adequacy”.
• “Receive Adequacy” keeps sensation as data.
• What changed: “Identify Part” → “Choose Non”?
• I can use “Receive Adequacy” while sensation stays.
rituals.formula_flow: Identify Part → Receive Adequacy → Choose Non
rituals.safety:
PAUSE

rituals.title: CHANGE ONE THING, WATCH ONE FEELING
rituals.goal: Two feelings untangle when one scene change moves only one of them.
rituals.steps:
1. Name Pair — Name two emotions in the mixture and rate each with a simple low, medium, or high—not a number.
2. Hold Scene — Hold the scene steady. Choose only one variable to test: person, time, place, audience, or outcome.
3. Swap Variable — Imagine that one variable changed for ten seconds. Keep every other fact the same.
4. Tag Driver — Notice which emotion moved and which stayed. Tag the changed variable as a likely driver, not a final explanation.
rituals.win: ✓ Noticed which emotion moved and which stayed.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Tag Driver”; let wanting crest.
• If it flares, choose “Swap Variable”.
• “Swap Variable” keeps wanting off controls.
• “Name Pair” versus “Tag Driver”: what eased?
• I can use “Hold Scene” without obeying the urge.
rituals.formula_flow: Name Pair → Hold Scene → Swap Variable → Tag Driver
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not use imagined substitutions to rewrite trauma, deny facts, or continue once the scene becomes overwhelming or unreal.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: TWO CHAIRS, NO TELEPATHY
rituals.goal: Give both positions a voice without claiming either is fact.
rituals.steps:
1. Place Chairs — Place two chairs apart.
2. Speak Position — Speak from your position using first person.
3. Switch Chair — Move and answer as the other position, labelling imagination where knowledge is missing.
4. Return To Facts — Return to your chair and state what changed, what did not, and what real conversation may still be needed.
rituals.win: ✓ The next sentence can carry the boundary without carrying the fight.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Return To Facts”; soften the jaw.
• Loop back? Use “Switch Chair”.
• “Switch Chair” keeps clarity above heat.
• “Place Chairs” to “Return To Facts”: what loosened?
• I can use “Speak Position” without extra heat.
rituals.formula_flow: Place Chairs → Speak Position → Switch Chair → Return To Facts
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Avoid this alone for traumatic relationships or if role-switching feels disorganising.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: TELL IT AT THE SPEED OF SAFETY
rituals.goal: Disclosure should increase clarity, not steal control.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose Trustworthy — Choose a trustworthy listener and agree on time, confidentiality, and a stop signal.
2. Share — Share facts first, then feelings and meaning in manageable detail.
3. Pause Orient — Pause to orient between sections.
4. End Support — End with what support you want now—not what the listener guesses.
rituals.win: ✓ I told enough truth to gain clarity without giving away control.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “End Support”; loosen the label.
• Catch restart with “Pause Orient”.
• “Pause Orient” — the rule loosened.
• Before/after: “Choose Trustworthy” → “End Support”.
• I can use “Share” without becoming the label.
rituals.formula_flow: Choose Trustworthy → Share → Pause Orient → End Support
rituals.safety:
PAUSE

rituals.title: MAKE FEAR NAME A DEADLINE
rituals.goal: A warning must become testable before it can command you.
rituals.steps:
1. Pin Forecast — Restate the fear as one visible or audible prediction—not a vague catastrophe.
2. Set Clock — Give the prediction a real time window.
3. Score Odds — Set confidence on a 0–100 scale before checking anything.
4. Observe Safely — Use only a naturally occurring safe observation; never manufacture a test.
5. Update Odds — Hold the result and update confidence in either direction.
rituals.win: ✓ The next move no longer has to obey the loudest second.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Update Odds”; leave the forecast.
• On return: “Score Odds”.
• “Observe Safely” — fear isn’t fate.
• What lost power: “Pin Forecast” → “Update Odds”?
• I can use “Set Clock” while fear stays loud.
rituals.formula_flow: Pin Forecast → Set Clock → Score Odds → Observe Safely → Update Odds
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not test danger, invade privacy, or repeat the observation to chase certainty.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.content:
TITLE
MAKE FEAR NAME A DEADLINE

GOAL
A warning must become testable before it can command you.

RITUAL
1. Pin Forecast — Restate the fear as one visible or audible prediction—not a vague catastrophe.
2. Set Clock — Give the prediction a real time window.
3. Score Odds — Set confidence on a 0–100 scale before checking anything.
4. Observe Safely — Use only a naturally occurring safe observation; never manufacture a test.
5. Update Odds — Hold the result and update confidence in either direction.

WIN
✓ The next move no longer has to obey the loudest second.

• Exhale after “Update Odds”; leave the forecast.
• On return: “Score Odds”.
• “Observe Safely” — fear isn’t fate.
• What lost power: “Pin Forecast” → “Update Odds”?
• I can use “Set Clock” while fear stays loud.

FORMULA FLOW
Pin Forecast → Set Clock → Score Odds → Observe Safely → Update Odds

PAUSE
Do not test danger, invade privacy, or repeat the observation to chase certainty.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: GROUNDING ANCHOR RELAY
rituals.goal: Rotate before one cue becomes background noise.
rituals.steps:
1. Select Different — Select four anchors from different systems: visual line, distant sound, contact pressure, joint position.
2. Switch Getting — Spend a short interval with each and switch before getting used to it empties it.
3. Finish Channel — Finish on the channel that restored the clearest present contact.
rituals.win: ✓ One channel brought the present back into focus.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Finish Channel”; notice the room.
• Re-entry move: “Switch Getting”.
• “Switch Getting” proves the present returned.
• “Select Different” to “Finish Channel”: what loosened?
• I can use “Switch Getting” to return here.
rituals.formula_flow: Select Different → Switch Getting → Finish Channel
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Use fewer anchors if switching itself increases overload.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: THE FEELING UNDER THE FEELING ABOUT IT
rituals.goal: Secondary emotion may be wearing the crown.
rituals.steps:
1. Name Emotion — Spot the primary emotion and its trigger.
2. Finish About — Then finish: ‘About feeling this, I feel…’ Locate each in a different body area or colour.
3. State Needs — Offer the primary state what it needs before addressing shame, anger, or fear about having it.
rituals.win: ✓ The first feeling finally got care before the second one took over.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “State Needs”; let wanting crest.
• On return: “Finish About”.
• “Finish About” keeps wanting off controls.
• Difference check: “Name Emotion” → “State Needs”.
• I can use “Finish About” without obeying the urge.
rituals.formula_flow: Name Emotion → Finish About → State Needs
rituals.safety:
PAUSE

rituals.content:
TITLE
THE FEELING UNDER THE FEELING ABOUT IT

GOAL
Secondary emotion may be wearing the crown.

RITUAL
1. Name Emotion — Spot the primary emotion and its trigger.
2. Finish About — Then finish: ‘About feeling this, I feel…’ Locate each in a different body area or colour.
3. State Needs — Offer the primary state what it needs before addressing shame, anger, or fear about having it.

WIN
✓ The first feeling finally got care before the second one took over.

• Exhale after “State Needs”; let wanting crest.
• On return: “Finish About”.
• “Finish About” keeps wanting off controls.
• Difference check: “Name Emotion” → “State Needs”.
• I can use “Finish About” without obeying the urge.

FORMULA FLOW
Name Emotion → Finish About → State Needs

PAUSE
Seek help if peeling exposes overwhelming trauma or self-attack.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: HALF-SPEED THE FIRST MOVE
rituals.goal: Slow the first move enough to catch the launch.
rituals.steps:
1. Identify Earliest — Catch the first movement linked to the urge—turning, reaching, standing, typing.
2. Observe Direction — do only that movement at half speed while observing its direction and tension.
3. Pause Completion — Pause at completion and decide whether the second movement serves you.
rituals.win: ✓ Slowing the launch exposed the choice before the second move fired.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Pause Completion”; mark the pause.
• If it flares, choose “Observe Direction”.
• “Observe Direction” proves choice interrupted habit.
• “Pause Completion”: what changed from “Identify Earliest”?
• I can use “Observe Direction” before autopilot.
rituals.formula_flow: Identify Earliest → Observe Direction → Pause Completion

rituals.title: DISASSEMBLE THE ALARM PANEL
rituals.goal: The whole alarm does not need to stop before one dial can move.
rituals.steps:
1. Read Channels — Read three channels without searching your whole body: SPEED, PRESSURE, and TEMPERATURE. Use lower, medium, or high.
2. Pick Smallest — Choose the safest channel with the lowest intensity. Do not pick the loudest one.
3. Move Dial — Move only that channel one step: slow one hand movement, soften one contact point, or adjust one safe layer of warmth or coolness.
4. Check Panel — Check whether that channel changed at all. Let the other two channels remain exactly as they are.
rituals.win: ✓ The alarm panel stopped behaving like one fused signal.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Check Panel”; then keep moving.
• Return once to “Move Dial”.
• “Move Dial” proves motion is available.
• At “Check Panel”, compare “Read Channels”.
• I can use “Pick Smallest” before motivation.
rituals.formula_flow: Read Channels → Pick Smallest → Move Dial → Check Panel
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
New, severe, or unusual physical symptoms require medical assessment. Stop for pain, faintness, breathing difficulty, confusion, or loss of orientation.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.content:
TITLE
DISASSEMBLE THE ALARM PANEL

GOAL
The whole alarm does not need to stop before one dial can move.

RITUAL
1. Read Channels — Read three channels without searching your whole body: SPEED, PRESSURE, and TEMPERATURE. Use lower, medium, or high.
2. Pick Smallest — Choose the safest channel with the lowest intensity. Do not pick the loudest one.
3. Move Dial — Move only that channel one step: slow one hand movement, soften one contact point, or adjust one safe layer of warmth or coolness.
4. Check Panel — Check whether that channel changed at all. Let the other two channels remain exactly as they are.

WIN
✓ The alarm panel stopped behaving like one fused signal.

• Exhale after “Check Panel”; then keep moving.
• Return once to “Move Dial”.
• “Move Dial” proves motion is available.
• At “Check Panel”, compare “Read Channels”.
• I can use “Pick Smallest” before motivation.

FORMULA FLOW
Read Channels → Pick Smallest → Move Dial → Check Panel

PAUSE
New, severe, or unusual physical symptoms require medical assessment. Stop for pain, faintness, breathing difficulty, confusion, or loss of orientation.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: BLANK THE NAMEPLATE
rituals.goal: Cover the label and see what you choose without it.
rituals.steps:
1. Picture Identity — Picture the identity label on a removable card and turn it face down.
2. Decision — For the next decision, refer only to capacities, needs, facts, and values.
3. Choose Shift — Choose.
4. Uncover Name — Then uncover the label and compare what it would have predicted.
rituals.win: ✓ The label went dark. The choice still appeared.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Uncover Name”; loosen the label.
• Pulled back? Touch “Choose Shift”.
• “Choose Shift” — the rule loosened.
• What lost power: “Picture Identity” → “Uncover Name”?
• I can use “Decision” without becoming the label.

rituals.title: EXIST FOR ONE MINUTE WITHOUT AUTOBIOGRAPHY
rituals.goal: Ongoing sense can be sensed before the life story is consulted.
rituals.steps:
1. Don't Recall — For sixty seconds, do not recall name, history, status, or plans.
2. Stay Changing — Stay with changing sound, pressure, light, and movement.
3. Simple — Notice the simple ongoing sense of being present through those changes.
4. End Reclaim — Reclaim your biography on purpose at the end.
rituals.win: ✓ For one minute, existence did not need a biography.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “End Reclaim”; loosen the label.
• On return, repeat “Simple”.
• “Simple” — the rule loosened.
• “Don't Recall” → “End Reclaim”: what changed?
• I can use “Stay Changing” without becoming the label.
rituals.formula_flow: Don't Recall → Stay Changing → Simple → End Reclaim
rituals.safety:
PAUSE

rituals.title: RETURN THEIR ACTION; KEEP YOUR CHOICE
rituals.goal: What someone did is not your identity property.
rituals.steps:
1. Imagine Three Boxes — Imagine three boxes: THEIR BEHAVIOUR; WHAT I LEARNED; WHAT I CHOOSE NOW.
2. Keep Each Part — Keep each thought in the right box.
3. Skip Forced Forgiveness — Forgiveness is not required on command.
4. Act From Choice — Take one action from the third box.
rituals.win: ✓ The surge has a shape now instead of filling everything.
rituals.supports:
• Gently exhale after “Act From Choice”; no breath-holding.
• On return: “Skip Forced Forgiveness”.
• “Skip Forced Forgiveness” — alarm isn’t command.
• Look back: “Imagine Three Boxes” → “Act From Choice”.
• I can use “Keep Each Part” while alarm rises.
rituals.formula_flow: Imagine Three Boxes → Keep Each Part → Skip Forced Forgiveness → Act From Choice

rituals.title: MEMORY REVIEW BY APPOINTMENT ONLY
rituals.goal: Choose when to revisit a memory instead of replaying it all day.
rituals.steps:
1. Set Limited — Set a limited review window and catch the reason for revisiting.
2. Add Keyword — When replay appears outside it, add one keyword to the Notice and redirect to present activity.
3. Remain Appointment — At the appointment, process purposefully or cancel if no useful aim remains.
rituals.win: ✓ The memory got an appointment instead of the whole day.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Remain Appointment”; drop the scoreboard.
• Loop back? Use “Add Keyword”.
• “Add Keyword” keeps worth off scoreboards.
• “Set Limited” to “Remain Appointment”: what loosened?
• I can use “Add Keyword” without ranking my worth.
rituals.formula_flow: Set Limited → Add Keyword → Remain Appointment

rituals.title: MATCH THE TASK TO THE BODY’S TEMPERATURE
rituals.goal: Action fails when stimulation and state are badly paired.
rituals.steps:
1. Read Body — Read current body alarm as lower, middle, or high.
2. Select Work — Select work with matching demand: energising movement for low, steady production for medium, simple contained tasks for high.
3. Reassess — Reassess after one unit and change lanes if needed.
rituals.win: ✓ I matched the task to the body I actually had today.
rituals.supports:
• One exhale after “Reassess”; keep moving.
• Restart detected: “Select Work”.
• “Select Work” proves motion is available.
• Before/after: “Read Body” → “Reassess”.
• I can use “Select Work” before motivation.
rituals.formula_flow: Read Body → Select Work → Reassess
rituals.safety:
PAUSE

rituals.title: THE VERSION THAT STILL COUNTS
rituals.goal: Perfection should not be allowed to cancel function.
rituals.steps:
1. Name Task — Name the task’s essential purpose.
2. Remove Feature — Remove every feature not required for that purpose.
3. Build Smallest — Build the smallest deliverable that still works, submit or finish it, then upgrade only if time and value justify the addition.
rituals.win: ✓ I built the smallest version that still counted, finished it, and left upgrades optional.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Build Smallest”; release the score.
• Shortcut: “Remove Feature”, once.
• “Remove Feature” keeps progress moving imperfectly.
• Before/after: “Name Task” → “Build Smallest”.
• I can use “Remove Feature” without perfecting.
rituals.formula_flow: Name Task → Remove Feature → Build Smallest
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Maintain full standards for safety-critical, clinical, legal, or hard to undo work.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.goal: Delayed outcomes train weakly; immediate feedback can bridge the gap.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose Small — Choose a small healthy reward delivered right after the process action, regardless of final result: music, a short break, a pleasant drink, or a brief message.

• Loop back? Use “Name the Reward”.
• “Choose Small” keeps blame in proportion.
• Compare “Choose Small” with “Name the Reward”.
• I can use “Name the Reward” without owning everything.

rituals.title: TURN DOWN ONE DOOR, NOT THE WHOLE HOUSE
rituals.goal: A boundary can close one door without burning down the whole house.
rituals.steps:
1. Name Contact — Name the contact pattern you want to change without judging the person.
2. Pick Door — Choose exactly one access door: TIME, TOPIC, CHANNEL, LOCATION, or FREQUENCY.
3. Lower One — Lower that door by one clear level: shorter call, one topic excluded, text only, public place, or fewer contacts.
4. Hold Setting — State the new setting and leave every other door unchanged for this round.
rituals.win: ✓ My part is clearer, and the rest is not mine to carry.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Hold Setting”; release extra load.
• If it flares, choose “Lower One”.
• “Lower One” keeps responsibility proportionate.
• At “Hold Setting”, compare “Name Contact”.
• I can use “Pick Door” without carrying it all.
rituals.formula_flow: Name Contact → Pick Door → Lower One → Hold Setting
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
If there is abuse, stalking, coercion, violence, or immediate danger, prioritise safety planning and professional support over gradual access changes.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.Final Consumer Ritual:
TITLE
TURN DOWN ONE DOOR, NOT THE WHOLE HOUSE

GOAL
A boundary can close one door without burning down the whole house.

RITUAL
1. Name Contact — Name the contact pattern you want to change without judging the person.
2. Pick Door — Choose exactly one access door: TIME, TOPIC, CHANNEL, LOCATION, or FREQUENCY.
3. Lower One — Lower that door by one clear level: shorter call, one topic excluded, text only, public place, or fewer contacts.
4. Hold Setting — State the new setting and leave every other door unchanged for this round.

WIN
✓ My part is clearer, and the rest is not mine to carry.

• Exhale after “Hold Setting”; release extra load.
• If it flares, choose “Lower One”.
• “Lower One” keeps responsibility proportionate.
• At “Hold Setting”, compare “Name Contact”.
• I can use “Pick Door” without carrying it all.

FORMULA FLOW
Name Contact → Pick Door → Lower One → Hold Setting

PAUSE
If there is abuse, stalking, coercion, violence, or immediate danger, prioritise safety planning and professional support over gradual access changes.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: TAKE UP 5% MORE SPACE
rituals.goal: Social threat often folds the body before any decision is made.
rituals.steps:
1. Widen Feet — Widen feet, elbows, chest, or seating position by a small manageable amount.
2. Keep Change — Keep the change below performance or dominance.
3. Observe Shape — Observe what the expanded shape signals internally and which words become easier to access.
rituals.win: ✓ Five percent more space unlocked words that threat posture was hiding.
rituals.supports:
• Gently exhale after “Observe Shape”; no breath-holding.
• Restart detected: “Keep Change”.
• “Keep Change” — alarm isn’t command.
• “Widen Feet” versus “Observe Shape”: what eased?
• I can use “Keep Change” while alarm rises.
rituals.formula_flow: Widen Feet → Keep Change → Observe Shape

rituals.title: SETTLE WITHOUT USING BREATH
rituals.goal: When respiration is a trigger, use other doors.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose Pressure — Choose pressure from a surface, steady gaze, mild temperature, and slow movement.
2. Check Sequence — Sequence them without checking breathing.
3. Choose the Channel — Notice which channel restores the clearest orientation to your current setting and keep only that one for the final interval.
rituals.win: ✓ I found a settling door that did not require touching the breath.
rituals.supports:
• Gently exhale after “Choose the Channel”; no breath-holding.
• Pulled back? Touch “Check Sequence”.
• “Check Sequence” — alarm isn’t command.
• Before/after: “Choose Pressure” → “Choose the Channel”.
• I can use “Check Sequence” while alarm rises.
rituals.formula_flow: Choose Pressure → Check Sequence → Choose the Channel
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Use medical care for breathing symptoms rather than on purpose ignoring them.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: UNWIND IN REVERSE
rituals.goal: Release the body by retracing its body alarm order backward.
rituals.steps:
1. Recall Muscle — Recall which muscle group tightened last.
2. Soften Work — Soften it first, then work back toward the first area that braced.
3. Pause Handoff — Pause between groups to feel the handoff.
4. Finish Original — Finish at the original starting point and compare the whole chain.
rituals.win: ✓ Retracing the alarm backward taught the body how to unwind forward.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Finish Original”; mark the pause.
• Restart detected: “Pause Handoff”.
• “Pause Handoff” proves choice interrupted habit.
• Keep one lesson: “Recall Muscle” → “Finish Original”.
• I can use “Soften Work” before autopilot.

rituals.title: WHICH WAY DOES THE URGE POINT?
rituals.goal: Body alarm becomes clearer when given a vector.
rituals.steps:
1. Act Classify — Without acting, classify the bodily impulse as toward, away, against, downward, upward, or still.
2. Body — Notice the body region carrying the arrow.
3. Ask Safe — Ask what safe action could honour the information without blindly completing the vector.
rituals.win: ✓ The urge found a direction without becoming an order.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Ask Safe”; leave the forecast.
• Pulled back? Touch “Body”.
• “Body” — fear isn’t fate.
• “Ask Safe”: what changed from “Act Classify”?
• I can use “Body” while fear stays loud.
rituals.formula_flow: Act Classify → Body → Ask Safe
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Create distance and support if the vector involves violence or self-harm.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: FIND FIVE COLOURS WITHOUT CHASING THEM
rituals.goal: Threat scanning narrows the palette.
rituals.steps:
1. Keep Body — Keep your body still enough for safety and locate five distinct colours across the scene.
2. Name Shade — Name shade and location, not emotional meaning.
3. Don't Move — Do not move toward pleasant colours or away from unpleasant ones.
4. Finish Colour — Finish with the colour farthest from the trigger.
rituals.win: ✓ Five colours pulled attention out of the chase and back into the scene.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Finish Colour”; notice the room.
• Skip replay; use “Don't Move”.
• “Don't Move” proves the present returned.
• At “Finish Colour”, compare “Keep Body”.
• I can use “Name Shade” to return here.
rituals.formula_flow: Keep Body → Name Shade → Don't Move → Finish Colour
rituals.safety:

rituals.title: LET ONE TASTE FINISH
rituals.goal: Consumption slows when flavour is followed to zero.
rituals.steps:
1. Take Small — Take one small bite or sip.
2. Track Taste — Track taste from first contact through peak, transformation, and complete disappearance.
3. Don't Add — Do not add another until the original flavour has ended.
4. Watch Wanting — Notice the exact point where wanting separates from tasting.
rituals.win: ✓ The taste ended; wanting did not have to chase it.
rituals.supports:
• One exhale after “Watch Wanting”; redirect attention.
• Use “Don't Add” on return.
• “Don't Add” proves one signal leads.
• At “Watch Wanting”, compare “Take Small”.
• I can use “Track Taste” amid noise.
rituals.formula_flow: Take Small → Track Taste → Don't Add → Watch Wanting
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not use for restrictive eating or where clinical nutrition guidance differs.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.Final Consumer Ritual:
TITLE
LET ONE TASTE FINISH

GOAL
Consumption slows when flavour is followed to zero.

RITUAL
1. Take Small — Take one small bite or sip.
2. Track Taste — Track taste from first contact through peak, transformation, and complete disappearance.
3. Don't Add — Do not add another until the original flavour has ended.
4. Watch Wanting — Notice the exact point where wanting separates from tasting.

WIN
✓ The taste ended; wanting did not have to chase it.

• One exhale after “Watch Wanting”; redirect attention.
• Use “Don't Add” on return.
• “Don't Add” proves one signal leads.
• At “Watch Wanting”, compare “Take Small”.
• I can use “Track Taste” amid noise.

FORMULA FLOW
Take Small → Track Taste → Don't Add → Watch Wanting

PAUSE
Do not use for restrictive eating or where clinical nutrition guidance differs.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: THE ROOM HAS JOBS, NOT DEMANDS
rituals.goal: A room becomes lighter when objects return to jobs instead of accusations.
rituals.steps:
1. Scan Objects — Choose four safe visible objects without moving toward them. Avoid screens if they add strain.
2. Name Jobs — For each object, name only its ordinary job: chair supports, lamp lights, cup holds, door opens.
3. Drop Demands — Say ‘not needed now’ to every function that does not serve the current safe moment. Do not remove or organise anything.
4. Choose Helper — Choose the one object whose real function supports what you can do now, then use only that function.
rituals.win: ✓ The room went back to having jobs instead of demands.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Choose Helper”; release extra blame.
• On return, repeat “Drop Demands”.
• “Drop Demands” keeps blame in proportion.
• Compare “Scan Objects” with “Choose Helper”.
• I can use “Name Jobs” without owning everything.
rituals.formula_flow: Scan Objects → Name Jobs → Drop Demands → Choose Helper
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Stop for visual pain, dizziness, nausea, disorientation, compulsive scanning, or any real emergency requiring immediate action.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: QUARANTINE THE UNAVAILABLE VARIABLE
rituals.goal: Analysis cannot solve what depends on a condition that does not exist.
rituals.steps:
1. Name Variable — Name the exact variable outside present control—another person’s decision, test result, future opening, missing resource.
2. State Change — State what change would make processing useful.

rituals.title: GIVE THE THOUGHT A RETURN ADDRESS
rituals.goal: Recurring concerns keep roaming when no destination exists.
rituals.steps:
1. Assign Concern — Assign the concern to one place: a named person, calendar slot, document, task name, or deliberate release.
2. Route Address — Say the address in your mind and route the thought there each time it returns.
3. Mark Undeliverable — If no useful address exists, mark the thought UNDELIVERABLE and let it pass without rerouting.
rituals.win: ✓ No useful address. That thought can stop roaming.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Mark Undeliverable”; mark the pause.
• Restart detected: “Route Address”.
• “Route Address” proves choice interrupted habit.
• What lost power: “Assign Concern” → “Mark Undeliverable”?
• I can use “Route Address” before autopilot.
rituals.formula_flow: Assign Concern → Route Address → Mark Undeliverable
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not redirect warning thoughts that require immediate evaluation.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: PUT THE PROMISE AT THE CROSSROADS
rituals.goal: A private intention is weakest where renegotiation begins.
rituals.steps:
1. Identify Decision — Spot the exact decision moment and place a visible or mental commitment there: a door cue, calendar alert, prepared object, or agreed reminder.
2. State Action — Make the cue name the exact action, not a motivational slogan.
3. Meet the Crossroads — When that decision point arrives, follow the cue before renegotiation begins.
rituals.win: ✓ I put the promise exactly where renegotiation usually starts.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Meet the Crossroads”; release extra blame.
• Loop back? Use “State Action”.
• “State Action” keeps blame in proportion.
• What changed: “Identify Decision” → “Meet the Crossroads”?
• I can use “State Action” without owning everything.

rituals.title: FIND YOUR WORKING GEAR
rituals.goal: Motivation can guess; one work pulse can measure.
rituals.steps:
1. Run Pulse — Choose one ordinary task and run it for exactly thirty seconds without trying to finish it.
2. Full Stop — Stop completely for fifteen seconds. Hands off, eyes away, and no planning the next move.
3. Read Strain — Rate actual strain as light, workable, heavy, or stop. Compare it with what you predicted before starting.
4. Set Gear — Choose the next gear—30/15, 60/30, or stop—and complete exactly one more cycle at that ratio.
rituals.win: ✓ One work pulse found the gear motivation could only guess at.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Set Gear”; release extra blame.
• Loop back? Use “Read Strain”.
• “Read Strain” keeps blame in proportion.
• At “Set Gear”, compare “Run Pulse”.
• I can use “Full Stop” without owning everything.
rituals.formula_flow: Run Pulse → Full Stop → Read Strain → Set Gear
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Stop for pain, illness, exhaustion, agitation, compulsive timing, or any task where interruptions create safety risk.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.Ritual Steps:
1. Run Pulse — Choose one ordinary task and run it for exactly thirty seconds without trying to finish it.
2. Full Stop — Stop completely for fifteen seconds. Hands off, eyes away, and no planning the next move.
3. Read Strain — Rate actual strain as light, workable, heavy, or stop. Compare it with what you predicted before starting.
4. Set Gear — Choose the next gear—30/15, 60/30, or stop—and complete exactly one more cycle at that ratio.

rituals.title: HARVEST THE PROOF OF PROGRESS
rituals.goal: Gains must be stored before motivation can spend them.
rituals.steps:
1. Create Prior — Collect three concrete differences created by prior effort—speed, quality, recovery time, knowledge, frequency, distance.
2. Date Examples — Attach dates or examples.
3. Choose Action — Select the one doable step that becomes reasonable because one difference now exists.
rituals.win: ✓ Progress became stored evidence instead of a feeling I could forget.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Choose Action”; release extra blame.
• If it flares, choose “Date Examples”.
• “Date Examples” keeps blame in proportion.
• “Create Prior” → “Choose Action”: what changed?
• I can use “Date Examples” without owning everything.
rituals.formula_flow: Create Prior → Date Examples → Choose Action
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not cherry-pick progress to ignore deteriorating health or strategy.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: FIVE CLUES MAY BE ONE CLUE
rituals.goal: Several clues can be one echo wearing different clothes.
rituals.steps:
1. Name Clues — Name up to five clues currently supporting the worried conclusion.
2. Link Sources — Imagine a line between clues that came from the same person, event, article, assumption, mood, or repeated retelling.
3. Collapse Copies — Collapse every linked cluster into one source family; do not count its echoes separately.
4. Recheck Claim — Recheck the claim using the number and quality of independent families that remain.
rituals.win: ✓ Five clues stopped pretending to be five independent witnesses.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Recheck Claim”; watch the thought.
• Re-entry move: “Collapse Copies”.
• “Collapse Copies” proves thought is observable.
• What lost power: “Name Clues” → “Recheck Claim”?
• I can use “Link Sources” without obeying thought.

1. Name Clues — Name up to five clues currently supporting the worried conclusion.
2. Link Sources — Imagine a line between clues that came from the same person, event, article, assumption, mood, or repeated retelling.
3. Collapse Copies — Collapse every linked cluster into one source family; do not count its echoes separately.
4. Recheck Claim — Recheck the claim using the number and quality of independent families that remain.

WIN
✓ Five clues stopped pretending to be five independent witnesses.

• Exhale after “Recheck Claim”; watch the thought.
• Re-entry move: “Collapse Copies”.
• “Collapse Copies” proves thought is observable.
• What lost power: “Name Clues” → “Recheck Claim”?
• I can use “Link Sources” without obeying thought.

FORMULA FLOW
Name Clues → Link Sources → Collapse Copies → Recheck Claim

PAUSE
Do not collapse separate danger signs or ignore qualified medical, legal, financial, or safety evidence.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: ONE LOCAL REASON
rituals.goal: Global meaning may be unavailable; today’s significance can still exist.
rituals.steps:
1. Find Anchor — Search only within the next twenty-four hours for one person, place, promise, task, or act that matters.
2. Name Reason — Name why it matters locally.
3. Invest Time — Give it ten minutes of undivided behaviour.
rituals.win: ✓ Feeling and fact took separate seats. The room got bigger.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Invest Time”; let feeling settle.
• Pulled back? Touch “Name Reason”.
• “Name Reason” separates feeling from fact.
• Keep one lesson: “Find Anchor” → “Invest Time”.
• I can use “Name Reason” while emotion stays loud.

rituals.title: CARRY FORWARD WITHOUT CALLING IT GOOD
rituals.goal: Pain can stay true while your response still belongs to you.
rituals.steps:
1. State Clearly — State clearly what was wrong or unwanted.
2. Name Boundary — Then name one boundary, skill, loyalty, or value you can carry forward without claiming the event was beneficial.
3. Let Value — Let the value belong to you, not to the harm.
rituals.win: ✓ The load shrank to the piece that truly belongs here.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Let Value”; release extra load.
• Shortcut: “Name Boundary”, once.
• “Name Boundary” keeps responsibility proportionate.
• “State Clearly” to “Let Value”: what loosened?
• I can use “Name Boundary” without carrying it all.
rituals.formula_flow: State Clearly → Name Boundary → Let Value
rituals.safety:

rituals.title: THE LAST-DAY FILTER
rituals.goal: Finite life can expose counterfeit urgency.
rituals.steps:
1. Imagine Back — Imagine looking back from life’s end—not to frighten yourself, but to rank.
2. Demand — Which current demand disappears?
3. Remain Relationship — Which relationship, integrity choice, health need, or contribution remains?
4. Give Surviving — Give the surviving priority one concrete slot today.
rituals.win: ✓ Counterfeit urgency failed the last-day test; one real priority survived.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Give Surviving”; slow the clock.
• Loop back? Use “Remain Relationship”.
• “Remain Relationship” puts facts above speed.
• Keep one lesson: “Imagine Back” → “Give Surviving”.
• I can use “Demand” without rushing.
rituals.formula_flow: Imagine Back → Demand → Remain Relationship → Give Surviving
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Skip mortality reflection when it intensifies anxiety, grief, or self-harm thoughts.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: PAIN IS PRESENT; LIFE HAS OTHER DEPARTMENTS
rituals.goal: Suffering should not absorb the entire identity budget.
rituals.steps:
1. Describe Hurting — Say exactly what is hurting.
2. Continue Alongside — Then name three processes continuing alongside it: caring, learning, digesting, noticing, working, resting, relating.
3. Choose Small — Choose one small action from a continuing department without denying the pain.
rituals.win: ✓ Pain stayed real, and another department of life stayed open.
rituals.supports:
• Gently exhale after “Choose Small”; orient to now.
• On return: “Continue Alongside”.
• “Continue Alongside” moves memory toward then.
• Compare “Describe Hurting” with “Choose Small”.
• I can use “Continue Alongside” while staying in now.
rituals.formula_flow: Describe Hurting → Continue Alongside → Choose Small
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Obtain care when pain or distress needs direct treatment.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: GIVE THE BIG QUESTION A ROOM, NOT THE HOUSE
rituals.goal: Existential inquiry needs boundaries to coexist with living.
rituals.steps:
1. Set the Room — Choose a short time for the big question.
2. Bring One Question — think about one clear question and stop when the time ends. You do not require a final answer.
3. Return To Life — Then do one normal task that shows how you want to live now.
rituals.win: ✓ The big question got a room; the rest of life kept the house.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Return To Life”; watch the thought.
• On return, repeat “Bring One Question”.
• “Bring One Question” proves thought is observable.
• “Set the Room” versus “Return To Life”: what eased?
• I can use “Bring One Question” without obeying thought.
rituals.formula_flow: Set the Room → Bring One Question → Return To Life
rituals.safety:
PAUSE

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: NAME THE GUARANTEE YOU ARE SECRETLY BUYING
rituals.goal: Research may be serving emotional certainty, not information.
rituals.steps:
1. Finish Sentence — Finish this sentence: ‘If I keep checking, I hope to guarantee that…’ Ask whether any amount of data can provide that emotional promise.
2. Remain Demand — Gather only information that changes action; treat the remaining demand as uncertainty to carry.
rituals.win: ✓ Useful information ended where the guarantee-seeking began.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Remain Demand”; leave it unanswered.
• Pulled back? Touch “Remain Demand”.
• “Finish Sentence” keeps uncertainty carryable.
• “Finish Sentence” to “Remain Demand”: what loosened?
• I can use “Remain Demand” without a guarantee.
rituals.formula_flow: Finish Sentence → Remain Demand
rituals.safety:
PAUSE

rituals.title: WHERE EXACTLY IS THE OBSERVER?
rituals.goal: Test whether the witness has a fixed address.
rituals.steps:
1. Search Carefully — Search carefully for the boundary, size, and location of the one who observes.
2. Check Behind — Check behind the eyes, chest, head, and surrounding field.
3. Observe Found — Every found sensation is itself observed.
4. Rest Inability — Rest with the inability to locate a final point.
rituals.win: ✓ The sentence stayed, but it stopped being the whole self.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Rest Inability”; release extra load.
• Pulled back? Touch “Observe Found”.
• “Observe Found” keeps responsibility proportionate.
• Keep one lesson: “Search Carefully” → “Rest Inability”.
• I can use “Check Behind” without carrying it all.
rituals.formula_flow: Search Carefully → Check Behind → Observe Found → Rest Inability
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not continue if location inquiry provokes feeling unreal or detached from yourself.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: PUT THE COMMENTATOR IN THE CHEAP SEAT
rituals.goal: Let task feedback lead while self-opinion becomes background sound.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose Skill — Choose one familiar, low-risk task with clear external feedback.
2. Centre Feedback — Put sight, touch, sound, or the work result in the centre of attention.
3. Demote Voice — When self-commentary appears, let it continue faintly at the edge without answering or silencing it.
4. Finish Unit — Finish one complete task unit using feedback—not self-opinion—to make corrections.
rituals.win: ✓ Commentary moved to the cheap seat; the moment kept centre stage.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Finish Unit”; mark the pause.
• If it flares, choose “Demote Voice”.
• “Demote Voice” proves choice interrupted habit.
• “Finish Unit”: what changed from “Choose Skill”?
• I can use “Centre Feedback” before autopilot.
rituals.formula_flow: Choose Skill → Centre Feedback → Demote Voice → Finish Unit
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Stop if divided attention reduces accuracy or makes the activity unsafe.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: ROTATE THE OBSERVATION DECK
rituals.goal: Every viewpoint edits what becomes prominent.
rituals.steps:
1. Observe Moment — Observe the same moment from three positions: body-centred, environment-centred, and whole-field.
2. Spot Amplifier — Keep what each amplifies and hides.
3. Choose Position — Choose the position best suited to the upcoming task rather than declaring any one neutral.
rituals.win: ✓ Perspective became a tool for the task, not a claim of neutrality.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Choose Position”; watch the thought.
• Catch restart with “Spot Amplifier”.
• “Spot Amplifier” proves thought is observable.
• Keep one lesson: “Observe Moment” → “Choose Position”.
• I can use “Spot Amplifier” without obeying thought.
rituals.formula_flow: Observe Moment → Spot Amplifier → Choose Position
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Use a stable perspective when rotation increases disorientation or makes it harder to sense where you are.

rituals.title: THE MILLISECOND BEFORE THE NAME
rituals.goal: What you notice exists briefly before concept files it.
rituals.steps:
1. Look Touch — Look at or touch something ordinary.
2. Catch Bare — Catch the first bare instant before ‘cup,’ ‘cold,’ ownership, or preference appears.
3. Don't Freeze — Do not freeze it; simply recognise the order: contact, then concept.
4. Repeat Unnamed — Repeat with a sound.
rituals.win: ✓ A sound appeared before its label could grab it.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Repeat Unnamed”; watch the thought.
• Restart detected: “Don't Freeze”.
• “Don't Freeze” proves thought is observable.
• Look back: “Look Touch” → “Repeat Unnamed”.

rituals.goal: You are the landscape experiencing weather, not the storm’s legal name.
rituals.steps:
1. Map The Weather — Imagine pressure zones, temperature, movement direction, visibility, and a likely prediction using colours or symbols.

rituals.title: FOUR-CELL DECISION MATRIX
rituals.goal: Separate value from danger before emotion blends them.
rituals.steps:
1. Score Option — Score each option on value alignment, downside, reversibility, and learning.
2. Add Sentence — Add a sentence explaining every score.
3. Compare Patterns — Compare patterns rather than relying on the total alone.
4. Prefer Option — Favour the option with containable risk while important value is expressed.
rituals.win: ✓ Value and danger separated before either could rig the choice.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Prefer Option”; let feeling settle.
• Catch restart with “Compare Patterns”.
• “Compare Patterns” separates feeling from fact.
• What changed: “Score Option” → “Prefer Option”?
• I can use “Add Sentence” while emotion stays loud.
rituals.formula_flow: Score Option → Add Sentence → Compare Patterns → Prefer Option
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Use expert advice for high-stakes scoring assumptions.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: WHICH REGRET ARE YOU AVOIDING?
rituals.goal: Regret has four species with different advice.
rituals.steps:
1. Estimate Regret — For each option, estimate regret of action, inaction, delay, and self-betrayal.
2. Describe Future — Say the future scene behind the highest score.
3. Ask Regret — Ask which regret is reversible and which conflicts most with your values.
rituals.win: ✓ Regret split into types, and only one deserved to guide the choice.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Ask Regret”; keep the compass.
• On return, repeat “Describe Future”.
• “Describe Future” keeps meaning in motion.
• “Ask Regret”: what changed from “Estimate Regret”?
• I can use “Describe Future” while pain stays real.
rituals.formula_flow: Estimate Regret → Describe Future → Ask Regret
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not let imagined regret override present safety or evidence.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: REMOVE WHAT THE CHOICE WOULD ‘PROVE’
rituals.goal: Identity signalling can distort an otherwise practical decision.
rituals.steps:
1. Say About — Name what each option would supposedly say about you—successful, loyal, brave, weak, ordinary.
2. Cross Out — Strike through those identity messages mentally.
3. Check Again — Re-check only consequences, values, constraints, and evidence.
4. Notice Shift — Notice whether the preferred option changes.
rituals.win: ✓ Identity stepped out of the voting booth; the practical choice became clearer.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Notice Shift”; keep the compass.
• Catch restart with “Check Again”.
• “Check Again” keeps meaning in motion.
• “Notice Shift”: what changed from “Say About”?
• I can use “Cross Out” while pain stays real.
rituals.formula_flow: Say About → Cross Out → Check Again → Notice Shift
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Identity and community may be legitimate values; distinguish them from performance.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: WHOSE HANDWRITING IS ON THIS BELIEF?
rituals.goal: Inherited rules often feel like your own after the source fades.
rituals.steps:
1. Name Modelled — Name who modelled, rewarded, enforced, or normalised the belief.
2. Picture Original — Picture the original context and what compliance protected.
3. Ask Whether — Now check if current-you endorses it under present values and data.
rituals.win: ✓ I found the old handwriting and decided whether the rule still deserved my signature.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Ask Whether”; keep both sides.
• If it flares, choose “Picture Original”.
• “Picture Original” widens the evidence field.
• “Name Modelled” to “Ask Whether”: what loosened?
• I can use “Picture Original” before concluding.
rituals.formula_flow: Name Modelled → Picture Original → Ask Whether
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Avoid blaming cultures or individuals simplistically; systems transmit mixed messages.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: MOVE THE RULE BETWEEN WORLDS
rituals.goal: A rule must survive context before it earns the word universal.
rituals.steps:
1. State Rule — Picture the rule without naming who taught it.
2. Change Context — Place it in three contrasting settings—for example family, workplace, and friendship—with different power and consequences.
3. Compare Effects — Compare who is protected, restricted, or harmed in each setting.
4. Keep Core — Keep only the part that remains ethical and workable across contexts; notice the rest as conditional.
rituals.win: ✓ The rule kept its ethical core and lost its fake universality.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Keep Core”; keep both sides.
• Catch restart with “Compare Effects”.
• “Compare Effects” widens the evidence field.
• Difference check: “State Rule” → “Keep Core”.
• I can use “Change Context” before concluding.
rituals.formula_flow: State Rule → Change Context → Compare Effects → Keep Core
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Stop if the comparison turns into contempt for people or excuses unsafe or unlawful behaviour.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: CHANGE THE COMPARISON DENOMINATOR
rituals.goal: A distorted reference group can manufacture failure.
rituals.steps:
1. Name Mind — Name the group your mind selected.
2. Match Resources — Substitute a baseline matched on starting point, resources, time, responsibilities, and opportunity.
3. Compare Progress — Compare progress with context included.
4. Group Exists — If no fair group exists, use your own prior trajectory.
rituals.win: ✓ The comparison group lost power; my own trajectory became the ruler.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Group Exists”; drop the scoreboard.
• If it flares, choose “Compare Progress”.
• “Compare Progress” keeps worth off scoreboards.
• Keep one lesson: “Name Mind” → “Group Exists”.
• I can use “Match Resources” without ranking my worth.
rituals.formula_flow: Name Mind → Match Resources → Compare Progress → Group Exists
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not use context to deny areas where effort or repair is needed.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: DO ONE GOOD THING WITH NO APPLAUSE BUTTON
rituals.goal: Values can survive the absence of approval.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose Safe — do a low-risk act you endorse and do it without announcing, checking reactions, or fishing for extra certainty.
2. Let Discomfort — Let the discomfort of no feedback rise and change.
3. Review Quietly — Review the action by your values once it is done.
rituals.win: ✓ I did one good thing with no audience and it still counted.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Review Quietly”; leave it unanswered.
• Skip replay; use “Let Discomfort”.
• “Let Discomfort” keeps uncertainty carryable.
• Before/after: “Choose Safe” → “Review Quietly”.
• I can use “Let Discomfort” without a guarantee.
rituals.formula_flow: Choose Safe → Let Discomfort → Review Quietly
